# Platform and Organism of GEO Series GSE309890

## Abstract

This query resolved the sequencing platform and source organism for NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) Series GSE309890. Two tool calls were made against the GEO `gds` Entrez index: one retrieving the Series record by accession, and a second resolving the platform accession returned by that record. GSE309890 is registered under platform GPL24659, whose GEO Platform title is "Illumina HiSeq 4000 (Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655)". The organism field (`taxon`) is identical at both the Series and Platform levels: *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655. The Series is an expression profiling by high throughput sequencing study comprising 6 samples, split by title into 3 control replicates and 3 "adaptive evolution, 40day" replicates, linked to BioProject PRJNA1363958, with a public release date of 2026/02/01. The study concerns sertraline-associated antibiotic resistance emergence and pentose phosphate pathway rewiring in *E. coli*. No PubMed record is linked to the Series in GEO. The platform GPL24659 is shared by 460 samples across GEO, indicating it is a general-purpose platform definition rather than one created for this study. The result matters because platform identity fixes the read chemistry and read-length expectations for any reanalysis, and the strain-level taxon determines which reference genome and gene model a reanalysis must use.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** GEO Series records bundle a set of samples from one study and point to a Platform record (GPL accession) that defines the instrument and the reference organism against which the samples were measured. GSE309890 is a bacterial transcriptomic study of *Escherichia coli* examining whether the SSRI sertraline biases antibiotic resistance emergence through a shift of glucose flux from glycolysis into the pentose phosphate pathway, with transketolase A (tktA) as the named intervention point. Platform and organism are the two metadata fields that determine whether the deposited expression values can be reused.

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query. The GEO record explicitly reports no linked PubMed record; the tool noted this means no link is registered in GEO, typically an unpublished or not-yet-indexed study, and does not mean the study has no data.

**Knowledge Gap.** The user held only the Series accession. The Series summary record names a platform by accession alone (GPL24659), which does not itself state an instrument; resolving the instrument required a second lookup of the Platform record.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: report the sequencing platform and the source organism for GSE309890 from GEO's own metadata fields. Expectation where one applies: the taxon recorded on the Series should match the taxon recorded on the Platform, since GEO Platform definitions are organism-specific.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** The question is a metadata lookup on a single known accession, so the query was routed directly to GEO rather than to a federated dataset search. GEO is the authoritative source for a GSE accession's platform and taxon fields. A second call was required because the Series esummary reports the platform only as a GPL accession.

**Materials.**
- NCBI GEO, `gds` Entrez database, reached with the `geo_series` tool (two calls, both via `esummary.fcgi`).

**Procedures.**
1. `geo_series(accession="GSE309890")` — default `list_files=true`, which additionally listed the FTP supplementary directory.
2. `geo_series(accession="GPL24659", list_files=false)` — file listing suppressed, as only the Platform title was needed.

No filters, no free-text search, and no date restriction were applied. Accession-to-UID mapping was performed by the tool arithmetically (GSE309890 → UID 200309890; GPL24659 → UID 100024659), not by keyword search.

**Statistical Analysis.** No statistics were computed. All values are single-record field reads: `platform`, `taxon`, `experiment_type`, `sample_count`, `bioproject`, and `date_public` from the Series record, and `title`, `taxon`, `sample_count`, and `date_public` from the Platform record. The 3-versus-3 sample split is a count of the six `samples[].title` strings containing "control" versus "adaptive evolution", denominator 6.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. Records retrieved from GEO.**

| Field | GSE309890 (Series) | GPL24659 (Platform) |
|---|---|---|
| Entrez UID | 200309890 | 100024659 |
| Entry type | Series (GSE) | Platform (GPL) |
| Title | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback | Illumina HiSeq 4000 (Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655) |
| Taxon | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | (not populated) |
| Platform | GPL24659 | GPL24659 |
| Sample count | 6 | 460 |
| Public date | 2026/02/01 | 2018/02/26 |
| Linked PubMed IDs | 0 | 0 |
| BioProject | PRJNA1363958 | (not applicable) |

**Table 2. Samples in GSE309890.**

| GSM accession | Title | Group |
|---|---|---|
| GSM9284457 | E. coli, control,rep1 | control |
| GSM9284458 | E. coli, control,rep2 | control |
| GSM9284459 | E. coli, control,rep3 | control |
| GSM9284460 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep1 | adaptive evolution |
| GSM9284461 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep2 | adaptive evolution |
| GSM9284462 | E. coli, adaptive evolution, 40day, rep3 | adaptive evolution |

**Findings.**

- GSE309890 is registered under platform GPL24659. The GEO Platform title for GPL24659 is "Illumina HiSeq 4000 (Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655)".
- The organism in the `taxon` field of GSE309890 is *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655. The same value appears in the `taxon` field of GPL24659.
- The Series contains 6 samples. Three of six titles (50%) contain "control"; three of six (50%) contain "adaptive evolution, 40day".
- The experiment type is "Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing".
- GPL24659 carries 460 samples across GEO as a whole, against 6 in this Series.
- GPL24659 was made public 2018/02/26; GSE309890 has a public date of 2026/02/01.
- GSE309890 is linked to BioProject PRJNA1363958. No PubMed ID is linked.
- One supplementary file exists: `GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz`, 510K, last modified 2025-11-14 11:10.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** The objective is met. The platform is Illumina HiSeq 4000 and the organism is *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655. The hypothesis that the Series and Platform taxon fields would agree holds: both read *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655, so the strain designation is consistent and not an inference from the study title.

**Context.** The instrument name is carried in the Platform *title* string, not in a separate structured instrument field, so it is a submitter-composed label. The ratio of 6 study samples to 460 platform-wide samples confirms GPL24659 is a reusable platform definition registered in 2018, eight years before this Series' public date, and was not created for GSE309890. The strain-level taxon is consistent with the study's stated design, an adaptive evolution experiment in *E. coli* under sertraline, with a 40-day timepoint appearing in three sample titles.

**Limitations.** GEO's esummary returns metadata only; the tool stated the processed expression values are not retrievable from any E-utilities call and exist only in the FTP supplementary file. The Platform record's `experiment_type` and `summary` fields are empty, so read length, single- versus paired-end layout, and library protocol cannot be established from these two records. The instrument is asserted by the platform title alone; it was not independently confirmed against the SRA run metadata under PRJNA1363958. The absence of a linked PubMed ID is an absence of a registered link, not evidence the work is unpublished. The 3-versus-3 grouping is read from free-text sample titles, not from a structured design field.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** GSE309890 was run on Illumina HiSeq 4000 (GPL24659) using *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655. The next query worth running is a lookup of BioProject PRJNA1363958 in SRA, which would return per-run instrument model, library layout, and read counts, and would independently corroborate the HiSeq 4000 assignment taken here from the platform title.

## References

[1] NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus, Series GSE309890. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus, Platform GPL24659. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GPL24659
[3] NCBI E-utilities esummary, db=gds, id=200309890, version=2.0. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi
[4] NCBI E-utilities esummary, db=gds, id=100024659, version=2.0. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi
[5] GEO FTP supplementary directory for GSE309890. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/
[6] GEO FTP supplementary file GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz
[7] GEO FTP platform directory for GPL24659. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/platforms/GPL24nnn/GPL24659/

## Acknowledgments

Data were provided by the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus and retrieved through NCBI E-utilities. The underlying records were deposited by the submitters of GSE309890 and BioProject PRJNA1363958.
